record.paper_title: Some open questions in axion theory
record.original_question: Can one construct a viable cosmological model in which the QCD axion itself acts as the inflaton and QCD radiation generated through thermal friction sustains warm inflation, perhaps by finding an early-universe mechanism that makes the light quarks heavy enough to evade the chemical-potential obstruction from light fermions?

evidence.quote: This direction opens up many interesting research questions. A particularly compelling prospect is a model in which the QCD axion could be the inflaton, and QCD makes up the radiation that is sourced during inflation.
A mechanism that gives larger masses to light quarks in the early universe could potentially avoid these constraints.

artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work has made substantial progress on this question. A model of warm inflation using a heavy QCD axion as inflaton has been constructed in which Standard Model quark masses are enhanced during inflation and relax to their measured values afterwards (Berghaus et al., "Warm inflation with a heavy QCD axion", 2024). Counterarguments ("No warm inflation from a vanilla axion", 2024) claim that with vanilla light-quark content sphaleron heating cannot sustain warm inflation, while a 2025 work ("Warm inflation with the Standard Model") argues the light-fermion obstruction can be alleviated via Hubble dilution of chiral chemical potentials. The viability of a fully realistic model and reconciliation of these claims is still under active debate; the question is therefore partially solved rather than definitively settled.

status_evidence.title: Warm inflation with a heavy QCD axion
status_evidence.snippet: A heavy QCD axion acts as the warm inflaton; a model is constructed in which quark masses are much larger during inflation and relax to measured values afterwards.
status_evidence.claim: A heavy-QCD-axion warm inflation model with enhanced quark masses during inflation has been constructed.

status_evidence.title: No warm inflation from a vanilla axion
status_evidence.snippet: Argues sphaleron heating with a vanilla axion and Standard Model light quarks cannot sustain warm inflation.
status_evidence.claim: A no-go style argument indicates that without modifications, warm inflation from a QCD axion fails.

status_evidence.title: Warm Inflation with the Standard Model
status_evidence.snippet: Effects of light fermions are alleviated by Hubble dilution of their chiral chemical potentials.
status_evidence.claim: A proposal addressing the light-quark obstruction via Hubble dilution of chiral chemical potentials.
